correctness.rationale: For every positive initial state in the explicit invariant rectangle, direct ratio and reciprocal identities prove that x,y vanish while the sum of y_n diverges; a convex ratio contraction gives c<1 ray selection and c>=1 extinction of x/y. Cesàro yields all first-order constants. For c>1, the ratio power bound makes x summable and shows y-1/n summable, hence a finite positive limit of n^c x. At c=1, exact w=y/x increment and reciprocal expansion yield a summable error after removing (1+d)log n+d loglog n. Four critical identities were independently rederived in symbolic algebra; checker numerics are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The double-unit-growth boundary is a canonical codimension-two degeneracy of the model, for which linearized stability says only nonhyperbolic. The theorem classifies the whole positive local basin into power-law coexistence rays, an exact logarithmic selection threshold, and initial-dependent noninteger extinction exponents. The sharp universal d loglog n coefficient is a nontrivial second-order clock relevant to distinguishing near-critical ecological transients; no perturbation/global theorem asserted.
